channel.title: KPMG Suisse – Communiqués de presse
channel.description: Derniers communiqués de presse de KPMG Suisse

item.title: Vaud Tax Barometer – the “12%” initiative to ease the tax burden for many taxpayers
item.description: The initiative “12%” would reduce taxpayers’ overall burden and improve the canton’s position in intercantonal comparisons

item.title: KPMG Switzerland Appoints New Heads of Financial Services and Advisory
item.description: KPMG Switzerland appoints Nicolas Moser and Timo Knak to its Executive Board.

item.title: Swiss Hospitals Show Improved Financial Performance, but Investment Pressure Remains High
item.description: The financial situation of the Swiss hospitals, rehabilitation clinics, and psychiatric clinics included in the analysis improved in 2025.

item.title: Swiss private banks: record assets, but lower profits
item.description: Private banks in Switzerland increased their assets under management by 14% last year, reaching a new record of CHF 3.4 trillion.

item.title: Pascal Sprenger named new CEO of KPMG Switzerland
item.description: The partners of KPMG Switzerland have elected Pascal Sprenger as new CEO from 1 October 2026.

item.title: European Economic Outlook: growing risks to Europe’s economy – Switzerland comparatively resilient
item.description: KPMG’s latest European Economic Outlook shows that the renewed energy price shock is weighing on Europe’s economy.

item.title: Corporate tax: United States’ special status increases pressure on Switzerland
item.description: Further amendments to the global minimum tax, most notably in connection with the side-by-side system used by the US, pose risks for Switzerland as a location.

item.title: KPMG strengthens global collaboration with SAP as an SAP Global Strategic Service Partner to drive measurable client value
item.description: KPMG is expanding its collaboration with SAP through a strategic services partnership agreement.

item.title: Swiss M&A market in 2025: solid M&A year in a challenging economic environment
item.description: Featuring 502 M&A transactions and a deal volume of around USD 166.8 billion, the 2025 M&A year outperformed the previous year.

item.title: Bern Tax Monitor 2025
item.description: Corporate Tax: Canton of Bern continues to rank last

item.title: Swiss Real Estate Sentiment Index 2025
item.description: Despite its negative sentiment regarding the economy, the real estate sector is optimistic.

item.title: KPMG Switzerland announces Leadership Succession in Swiss Audit Practice
item.description: Michael Blume succeeds Lukas Marty as Head of Audit, effective 1 October 2025.

item.title: Swiss private banks: assets under management at record high
item.description: Private banks in Switzerland increased their assets under management by 14% last year, reaching a new record of CHF 3.4 trillion.

item.title: Corporate tax rates decline in Switzerland - global minimum tax and US tariffs top agenda
item.description: The average corporate tax rates for companies in Switzerland fell from 14.6 to 14.4 percent year over year.

item.title: Fraudsters: usually male, 36 to 55 years old and long-serving employees
item.description: The typical fraudster is male, between 36 and 55 years in age and has been with a company for more than six years.

item.title: Fewer mergers and acquisitions on the Swiss M&A market
item.description: With 464 mergers and acquisitions in 2024, 4 percent fewer transactions were conducted compared to 2023.

item.title: Tax competition: Canton of Bern under pressure
item.description: Corporate tax rates: The Canton of Bern still trailed the rankings in an intercantonal comparison conducted in 2024.

item.title: Real estate investment market – confidence returns
item.description: Positive price and market expectations have put the Swiss Real Estate Sentiment Index back in positive territory after an all-time low.

item.title: Private banks are thriving thanks to interest income
item.description: Small private banks in particular were able to improve their results and increase their gross profit by two thirds.

item.title: KPMG Switzerland and KPMG UK confirm merger
item.description: Partners at KPMG Switzerland and KPMG UK have voted in favor of merging their partnerships.

item.title: Global minimum tax: different strategies in the cantons
item.description: The introduction of the global minimum tax in Switzerland has already prompted a few cantons to revise their tax laws.

item.title: KPMG Switzerland joins SAP® PartnerEdge®
item.description: KPMG Switzerland and SAP bring together their market and digital expertise to offer industry-specific solutions and accelerate digital transformation.

item.title: Fewer mergers and acquisitions on the Swiss M&A market
item.description: At 484 mergers and acquisitions, 25 percent fewer transactions were conducted compared to 2022.

item.title: Canton of Vaud lagging behind on taxation of natural persons
item.description: The canton of Vaud has some of the heaviest income tax rates for natural persons among Switzerland's cantons.
